Honestly, I would give ARK: Survival Evolved 3 stars. The concept of the game is amazing, and the graphics are really good. I love the idea of surviving, exploring, taming dinosaurs, and being able to play with friends. However, the experience is frustrating when it comes to actually getting into the game. First and foremost, the game can be extremely laggy, and joining my friend's server is always a mission. I constantly find myself restarting my PC, trying over and over again to join through Steam, and wasting time just trying to get into the server. It shouldn't be this difficult to play a game with your friends.

I have about 18 hours in this game, 15 of which were wasted trying to connect to my friend. I was able to join once and we played for about 2 hours. Then, I disconnected for a few hours. Nothing had changed during that time, but I was never able to join him again. I have read and watched every single tutorial I could find on the internet. My other friends can join him, but I cannot. It is not the ISP or the firewall; we tried disabling every security measure on the modem and PC, on both the host's end and mine. We tried using Steam's server browser, but had no luck. We tried forwarding ports so I could join, but nothing worked. The host also cannot join the servers I create. We have the same version, and we both bought it on Steam. We are three friends who want to play together, but even if we change the host, there is always someone else who cannot join. Also, the game freezes a lot during launch for about 5 to 10 minutes on four different, decent systems.

My Steam hours don’t even come close to showing how much time I’ve actually spent with ARK. I have another 1,057 hours on Xbox. I loved this game enough that I literally scheduled vacation days around the release of new maps.

Some of my best memories were from the community and running my own dedicated server. Back before renting a server was an option, I had an old Xbox set up just to run ours. There was something really fun about having your own little community, building massive bases, exploring a new map together, and seeing what everyone came up with.

Base building and breeding dinos were easily two of my favorite parts of the game. I could spend an embarrassing amount of time working on a base or trying to breed better dinos.

Where ARK started losing me was when it moved further away from the dinosaur survival experience. Once things like mech suits and increasingly overpowered creatures started becoming a bigger part of the game, I didn’t enjoy the direction nearly as much. I preferred when surviving, building, taming, and breeding dinosaurs were really the heart of it.

Even with that complaint, I obviously can’t pretend I didn’t love ARK. Between Xbox and Steam, I’ve put well over 1,200 hours into it. Some games you play and move on from.
